stem: A chemical splashes into a client's eye at work. What should be done first after ensuring scene safety?

options.A: Begin immediate copious eye irrigation and continue while further evaluation is arranged
options.C: Patch the eye and delay irrigation until an ophthalmologist arrives
options.D: Attempt to neutralize the chemical with the opposite-pH solution

rationale: Ocular chemical exposure is an emergency in which time to irrigation strongly affects outcome. AAO EyeWiki guidance states that irrigation should begin immediately and should not be delayed for history or a complete examination. Neutralizing acid with alkali or vice versa can worsen injury; medications are considered after decontamination and assessment.
educational_objective: Prioritize immediate irrigation after ocular chemical exposure.
source_document_title: Chemical (Alkali and Acid) Injury of the Conjunctiva and Cornea
source_locator: Irrigation and Early Management; Bystanders/First Responders
source_claim_supported: Supports immediate copious irrigation without delaying for history/exam and avoidance of chemical neutralization attempts.
correction_summary: Removed unsupported fixed-duration wording from the stem and made immediate irrigation the unambiguous priority.
audit_findings: A is the emergency decontamination priority; B/C delay irrigation and D can worsen injury.
